source_references.title: How to recover from microservices
source_references.author: David Heinemeier Hansson
source_references.evidence_scope: Argues for consolidating tightly dependent service paths into a modular monolith and extracting services only when a clear boundary and justification exist.
source_references.notes: Source metadata and original paraphrase only; article language is not copied.

source_references.title: The Big Cloud Exit FAQ
source_references.author: David Heinemeier Hansson
source_references.evidence_scope: Documents cost, independence, workload-fit, staffing, and deployment considerations behind moving suitable workloads from public cloud services.
source_references.notes: Source metadata and original paraphrase only; financial claims are not generalized.

source_references.title: Our switch to Kamal is complete
source_references.author: David Heinemeier Hansson
source_references.evidence_scope: Describes standardizing container deployment across applications and preferring a small durable operational layer over a complex platform.
source_references.notes: Source metadata and original paraphrase only; implementation detail is not copied.

principles.statement: Keep tightly coupled application behavior in one deployable system until a concrete boundary and operational benefit justify distribution.
principles.evidence_note: The authored post recommends consolidation and modular separation before network separation.
context_dependencies: Web applications with tightly dependent request paths

signature_moves.statement: Standardize deployment through a small durable layer that can run the same application packaging across owned or rented servers.
signature_moves.evidence_note: The post describes a completed multi-application deployment standardization.

likely_objections.statement: Public cloud premiums and managed-service complexity require workload-specific justification rather than default acceptance.
likely_objections.evidence_note: The FAQ grounds the objection in a specific stable workload and operating model.

anti_patterns.statement: Splitting dependent application paths across services before clear boundaries emerge adds avoidable coordination and operational failure modes.
anti_patterns.evidence_note: The recovery account identifies cross-service dependency as the source of avoidable complexity.

context_dependencies: Apply to conventional web products and predictable server workloads; economics remain context-specific.

abstention_boundaries.reason: The selected evidence explicitly depends on workload shape and does not establish a universal cloud-exit rule.
The selected posts do not establish compliance suitability.

open_questions: At what workload profile does managed-cloud leverage outweigh its premium?
